issue_context.title: Android: stdout is set to `errors="surrogateescape"`
issue_context.body:
# Bug report

### Bug description:

The Android stdout and stderr tests include an assertion that both streams are set to `errors="backslashreplace"`, which is the most useful setting for redirecting the streams to the Android log. However, this test only passed because the CPython test harness reconfigures stdout – outside of the tests, it's set to `surrogateescape`.

### CPython versions tested on:

3.13

### Operating systems tested on:

_No response_

<!-- gh-linked-prs -->
### Linked PRs
* gh-125943
* gh-125950
<!-- /gh-linked-prs -->

review_comments: Not sure I understand what is going on here - why is the `errors` kwarg no longer required?
Because it's been added as a default in TextLogStream itself.
The idea is that because of how the output is being logged, we want to explicitly use backslashreplace, rather than copying the existing `errors` setting.
Got it - I was misreading what `sys.stdout.errors` was passing in.
